reasoning: The flow 10.1.100.10→10.1.200.10:5432 matches SID 9000001 which is classified P1 and maps to TA0008/T1021 remote services.
Policy matrix explicitly DENYs WEB→DB-OLTP, making any such flow a microsegmentation breach.
Baseline analysis shows no legitimate WEB→DB traffic; this flow is not part of known steady‑state patterns.
Historical enforcement data shows 6 prior identical SID alerts all resulted in DROP with confidence 0.93, indicating a recurring threat pattern.
Severity scoring adds +4 (cross_zone_policy_violation) +1 (dst_port_in_critical_db_set) =5 points → P1 tier, requiring DROP.
Confidence calibration (unambiguous signals, repeated enforcement) yields 0.93 (>0.85), satisfying hard‑override rule for DROP.
Targeted block (src/dst/port) limits blast radius while fully stopping the policy violation.
No hard‑override (MGT source) applies; source is WEB, so DROP is permitted.
TTL 3600s aligns with SID recommendation and ensures temporary mitigation while allowing later review.
